question: Which steps of a convoy's way the submarines' raidable tonnage counts.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits
addresses.comment:
**The theatre agent's fleets, every pass the tick allows.** Extent 0x4D0880-0x4D3EA1 (the throw tail past the real `ret 8` at 0x4D3E67). Gates: `!force && !at_war (+0xACC) && !in_undeclared_war (+0xACD)` returns; force clears +0x85; no fleet on +0xDC returns; the area is GetArea or the theatre of the unit's province, which must be ours. Phases in order: (1) 0x4D099D withdraw from a losing sea battle (slot-17 ratio against 0.5). (2) 0x4D0B30 **idle fleets home**: a fleet not moving, with no busy order (slot 24) and not at its own base is MoveUnit-ed to its base when CanUnitReach; but a fleet whose definition carries troops (transport_capability >= 1000) stays in port while the plan has an embark (CUnit +0x284); a fleet with no base or an unreachable one is kept on a 'homeless' vector. (3) 0x4D0D70 port and repair, and the 'ready' vector (FINDINGS-agents.md C.3). (4) 0x4D14F0 **existing orders**, per ready fleet: an idle fleet with no destination (+0x2CC) sitting in a port that is not its base is moved to its base, unless it holds a transport and lies in the plan's embark port; a busy fleet: join_fleet - the mover and its target go on the 'handled' list and the port tallies move; a busy transport fleet carrying nothing (CNavy +0x2EC) is cancelled unless CUnit +0x2CA is set; convoy_raid and convoy_escort are cancelled at peace, an escort also when its target is gone; patrol is kept only at war; any other order is kept while the fleet has a destination, cancelled at its own base, and an intercept with no destination away from base is cancelled; cancel = IssueUnitOrder(none) and MoveUnit to the base (or where it is). (5) 0x4D19F6 split and merge (C.3). (6) 0x4D2025 the handled fleets swap-removed from the ready vector (Vector_SwapRemoveValue, which reorders it); +0x27C and +0x280 zeroed; **enemy survey**: every naval unit of every country at war or in undeclared war with us within NavalDistanceTo 1000 of one of the theatre's ports and hostile where it stands (CCountry::IsEnemy) adds GetPower/1000 to +0x27C and goes on a local list, troop carriers (+0x2EC > 0) at the front, the rest at the back. (7) 0x4D2418 per ready fleet: submarine convoy raid, or relocation to the port with most raidable tonnage when fewer than half the route provinces seen are raid candidates, or a surface rebase; the tail adds a free fleet's GetPower/1000 to +0x280 and keeps it free (FINDINGS-airnaval4.md, and FINDINGS-moving.md D). (8) 0x4D323D **patrol**, with naval stance != 0 and (at war, undeclared war or +0x28C > 0): the region V = the +0x284 provinces, or failing any, the sea zone (+0xA4) of each theatre port, both less what CAIUnit_IsBalticBarredToAllies refuses; while V is not empty: centre = V[rand() % |V|] (the C runtime's rand, per thread), the patrol area the centre plus the nearest remaining V entries to it (up to five provinces, each swap-removed from V); the fleet = the nearest free fleet with no busy order, no submarine and at least one screen; `patrol` from now to now + 168 hours over that area; no fleet ends the phase. (9) 0x4D37EA **intercept**, per enemy fleet of the survey list at sea and not Baltic-barred, and only where enemy power (+0x27C) <= own power (+0x280) x 1.5 (2.0 at naval stance 1) unless it carries troops: need = its GetPower/1000, target = need (x 0.66 for a troop carrier); free fleets are gathered nearest first (NavalDistanceTo, strict, first of equals) while 2 x need > gathered, each reachable (CanUnitReach), of non-zero power, not on patrol unless the enemy carries troops, and with a screen when the enemy is all submarines; if gathered >= target, the first gets `intercept` on the enemy fleet and the rest `join_fleet` onto the first, each window now to now, own power reduced and need reduced by each until it falls below zero. Returns 'split or merged a fleet'; slot 73 ignores it.

**Read again 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 25). **After the split and merge, an unforced pass ends** (`cmp byte [ebp+0xC], 0` at 0x8D202B): the survey, the per-fleet raid and rebase, the patrol and the intercept run only when the pass is forced - the full pass or replan_naval - at war as at peace. Phase 4's raid, escort and patrol are kept when the country is at war **or in an undeclared war** (+0xACD), not at war alone: on the save of July 1941 the United States is in one, and its Pacific patrols are kept at peace for 48 hours. **Phase 7's tail, on the listing 2026-11-11** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 42): only a fleet holding no transport (CountShipsByRole out[1] < 1, 0x4D3146) goes on - its power added to +0x280 unless its order is 0x6DE, 0x6E5 or 0x6E9, and it is put on the free list ([esp+0x154], 0x4D3222) where order slot 24 is clear or its order is 0x42E or 0x6E8; the patrol and the intercept take fleets only from that list, so a fleet carrying a transport is sent on neither. **The patrol's rand measured 2026-11-12** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 53): drawn at 0x4D33E6 on the C runtime's per-thread stream - fresh worker threads from seed 1 (41, 18467, 6334), the main thread carrying on from every draw since the process began; entering July 1941 Germany, Britain, the Soviet Union and the United States drew on the main thread. **The split and merge read 2026-11-12** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 57): a fleet walked is passed over retreating, fighting, empty, handled, under a blocking order (0x4D1A9A) or away from its own base (0x4D1AA7); a fleet that split a ship off is pushed onto the handled vector at 0x4D1D29 and still looks for a partner; the merge asks fewer than 6 ships by the fleet's own count (+0x40, 0x4D1D45), the split ships not yet gone. **The rebase's entry and scoring, read on the listing 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 64): a fleet with no base, or whose base province's theatre (CMapProvince +0x380/+0x384) differs from the agent's theatre (CTheatre +8/+0xC, CObjectId_Differs at 0x4D2E25), is rebased whatever it holds; past that a submarine ends it; a base in another area than the commander's (CUnit +0x1E0 -> +0x130 -> +0x2B4) rebases too; else only a crowded base. The ports are the theatre's (+0x94) in the commander's area, scored by distance to the commander's province + 10.0, + 2000 a ship over the level, x0.75 for the own base; the departure is taken off the old base's arrivals. **The orders that no longer make sense, read on the listing 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 65): over each fleet, one with no blocking order (slot 0x60) is passed over while moving (+0x2CC); a join_fleet (0x6E5) is set aside; then a fleet holding a transport (ship definition +0x30), carrying nothing (+0x2EC) and with +0x2CA clear is cancelled whatever its order (0x4D1822); then raid and escort at peace, an escort whose convoy is gone, a patrol at peace, and for a fleet standing still an order at its base or an intercept. The cancel: IssueUnitOrder(none, 0x18D) at 0x4D19A8 and MoveUnit(fleet, base, 0, 0, 0, 0) at 0x4D19BD. **Phase 6, read on the listing 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 72; 0x4D2039-0x4D2072): the handled fleets' vector ([esp+0x68]) is walked in insertion order and each fleet taken out of the ready vector ([esp+0xB0]) by Vector_SwapRemoveValue, the last ready fleet moved into its place - so phase 7's rebases run over the reordered vector. Japan's Imperial General Headquarters at a new game's second hour: 14., 16., 20. Kaigun to 5346, 19. to 5218, 18. to 4986. **The handled vector's pairs** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 77): the fleet joined goes on before its joiner, in phase 4 and in the merge alike - read at 0x4D2039 for Home Command, '1st Destroyer Squadron, HMS Argus', '2nd Navy, 1st Navy'. **The fleetless return seen in the patrol draws** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 112): over twelve hours of July 1941 no country without fleets made a patrol draw, Yemen, Oman, Iraq, Bulgaria and Belgium among them. **Phase 7's raid, read on the listing and logged 2026-11-16** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 114): the half test is `candidates >= seen / 2` in whole numbers (0x4D28C4-0x4D28DA), so 10 of 21 raids; no candidates goes to the relocation. The relocation's berths are the units its naval base holds, a per-port tally (hash_map<int,int> at [esp+0x1A0]) and the fleet's own ships (+0x40) where the port is not its base; a rebase moves the fleet's ships in that tally from its base to the chosen port (0x4D2A6D-0x4D2AD2) and ends its turn, while an empty tonnage map (0x4D28FE) or a best port that is its own base (0x4D2A63) falls through to the draw - it raids anyway. **A fleet the surface rebase sends is neither counted nor free** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 128): where phase 7's best port is found and is not the fleet's base, the arrival tally moves (0x4D30E1-0x4D3127), IssueUnitOrder(rebase 0x6DE) is posted (0x4D313C) and the loop jumps to its end (0x4D3141 -> 0x4D3227), past CountShipsByRole, the power added to +0x280 and the free list (0x4D3146-0x4D3222); a best port that is the base, or none, falls through to them. So phases 8 and 9 cannot take a fleet rebased in the same pass, though its order is null until the command runs.

**Phase 7's raidable tonnage counts every step of a convoy's way** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 132; 0x4D2640-0x4D289A): a step that is an end of the way, one of 0x2927..0x292A or Baltic-barred is passed over; every other step reaches the tonnage pass at 0x4D2830 - one already a candidate directly (0x4D26BF, not counted as seen), one IsTargetInRange refuses after counting it seen (0x4D26DC), a new candidate after it is added - and only an undeclared-war opponent's step its war does not cover skips it (0x4D27DE). The pass adds GetDesiredTransports to each theatre port (CTheatre +0x94) whose NavalDistanceTo the step is strictly under the fleet's cached range (0x4D286D).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x8D2640-0x8D289A read 2026-11-18. The running game: a probe at 0x8D299B on 17 July 1941 10:00 gave the Soviet tonnage 906 10, 986 10, 820 8, 782 4, 46 3, 311 1, which OpenHOI3 built so reproduces port for port. Wrong if a port reached only from an out-of-range step ever scores nought.
